status: completed synthetic stress study; computation reviewed
question: How do copied reports and coupled source errors change an enumerated identity mapping?
outcome: 73,728 records over 48 new systems. In shifted administrative eight-code wrong-source conditions, ten copied reports yield 1/48 recovery and 46 confident errors; counting source once gives 25/48 and 11 errors; the coupled-swap model gives 41/48 and 4. One correct source B gives 45/48 and 0 errors for source-once models, while ten copies of A give 3/48 and 45 errors. Twelve checks and 18,432 independent row replays pass.
challenge: Exact copies and correlated mistakes supply different dependencies. Hard source disagreements can remove every candidate. Reused training sizes require system-level comparisons.
remedy: Explicit 29-state source channel, copied/source-once baselines, preserved empty sets, independent inverse-response likelihood and system-level paired bootstrap intervals.
retry_when: A new source-error family, measured source reliability, partial copying model or independently acquired archaeological quantity/identity relation changes the likelihood.

question: Which Harappa lower-face arrangement distinctions survive face exchange and end reversal?
outcome: Nineteen readable pairs occupy 8 displayed states. Exchangeable lower faces give 4 groups with counts 4,3,5,7; adding common reversal gives 11 same-side and 8 opposite-side objects; separate reversals give 1 group. Three unresolved pairs produce whole-frame bounds 11–14 and 8–11. Seven main checks and 9 independently reconstructed-source checks pass.
challenge: Published drawing rows lack an explicit oriented prism-face and common-end map. A and D inventory and native-raster refinements needed independent source reconstruction.
remedy: Declared each conditional representation before calculation, retained unresolved objects, reconstructed source fields and direct form-specific partitions without calling the orbit implementation.
retry_when: Adjoining-face photographs or 3D records identify physical ends, face order, incision orientation and damaged regions.
